name: The Wych Elm of Park Middenburg
access: Free, open at any hour. Park Middenburg/Sonnenburgh has been a public municipal park since the estate was bought by Voorburg council in 1952 (the manor house itself, now offices, is not open to visitors, but the tree stands on the open grass field, not near the house).
transport: Voorburg railway station (NS), short walk into the park; also reachable from The Hague centre by tram/bus in well under 30 minutes.
verify_notes: Day-trip addition to The Hague, next free id hag_033 (checked highest existing id in data/cities/the-hague.json: hag_032), 718m from hag_029 (The Copper Beech at the Voorburg Cemetery Gate), well within the city's existing Voorburg cluster. bomenbieb.nl: planted 1750, describes it as 'one of the oldest wych elms (ruwe iep) in the Netherlands', standing on the open grass field behind the former manor house within the old Middenburg estate (park history to 1657). monumentaltrees.com independently lists a Ulmus glabra at the same park/coordinate cluster, measured 20.40m tall on 31 July 2017 (figure from a WebSearch snippet only; the page itself returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch, so treat the height as indicative rather than fully verified against the live page) and possibly the cultivar 'Exoniensis' (Exeter Elm) rather than the wild type -- worth a note for the writer/reader question rather than a firm claim, since the bomenbieb name just says 'ruwe iep' (the ordinary Dutch name for the species). Age: bomenbieb's 1750 planting date is a round figure with no stated basis; treating it as a broad band (250-300y) rather than a precise 276y. Alive: no dead/removal report found in Dutch news or Wikipedia; monumentaltrees' 2017 measurement plus bomenbieb's 2026 harvest are the two most recent independent sightings and agree it stands. Wych elms are vulnerable to Dutch elm disease so this is worth a reader-input flag on the page (has anyone seen it lately) even though nothing suggests a problem.

name: The White Willow of Wilp

location.address: Bolwerksweg, along the IJssel dike near Wilp
location.neighbourhood: Wilp (Voorst), on the IJssel foreland near the A1 viaduct

access: Free, standing beside the public Bolwerksweg dike road, part of the 'Langs Wilp en IJssel' walking route (dwarsdoorsalland.nl) and visible from the A1 motorway bridge toward Deventer. The floodplain path itself may be seasonally closed to protect nesting birds (15 March-15 July per the Deventer floodplain plan), but the tree stands by the road/dike rather than deep in the floodplain, so it is not affected.
transport: No rail station nearby; reachable by bike or car along the Bolwerksweg from Deventer (roughly 2km/10-15 min cycle from dev_008 The Steenenkamer Maple on the same road), or bus toward Wilp village.
verify_notes: Day-trip/cluster addition to Deventer, next free id dev_009 (highest existing id in data/cities/deventer.json is dev_008, itself at 'Bolwerksweg 10' -- the same road, roughly 2km away, published in this same lead pile 2026-09-06). bomenbieb.nl (plural 'de bomen', suggesting more than one remarkable willow at this spot): planted 1890-1900, stands on a river ridge along the IJssel at Wilp, visible from the A1 bridge, with 'enormous twisted trunks' from decades without pollarding. rivierverhalen.nl (Salland regional river-heritage site) independently confirms and adds real measurements: circumference about 7 metres (girth_cm 700), hollow but vital trunk, still gaining roughly 10cm of girth a year, damaged by a lightning strike in the 1990s that took part of the stem and left it leaning. It also describes a second, three-stemmed old white willow standing next to this one, badly damaged by fire (arson or lightning) in autumn 2020 -- since the article discusses that 2020 damage, it was written afterward and both trees were still standing then; treat as the most recent independent sighting. monumentaltrees.com lists a schietwilg entry for the same spot ('IJssel nabij A1 viaduct', Wilp) corroborating location, though the page itself 403s automated fetches so only the URL/title is used, not any figures from it. This entry describes the 7m-girth willow as the primary tree per bomenbieb's singular name (schietwilg wilp); the neighbouring fire-damaged willow is a secondary detail for the story, not a second collectible point. Location precision: approximate -- bomenbieb gives a coordinate but the exact tree among the small willow group at this dike spot is not independently pinned, and this is farmland/foreland rather than a park, so 'the willows on the Bolwerksweg dike near the A1 viaduct' is the honest level of precision.
